memo:
### Position read
Opening position; Red has moved from (0,3) to central square (3,3). No losses or eliminations. The center is now our main spatial advantage, but the opponent can contest it from either side.

### Our plan
Use Yellow to claim a complementary center square, preferably (4,3) or (4,4), while developing same-color flanks that can punish opposing center occupants. Avoid friendly-fire lines through our mixed-color formation.

### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet.

### Lessons
A piece moving into a sandwich is safe; captures trigger only from the mover’s landing square. Same-color endpoints are required, so coordinate each color’s capture geometry independently.

### Position read
We hold central squares (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; the opponent holds (4,3) with Blue. No losses. Our Yellow on (4,4) threatens to capture that Blue by later landing another Yellow on (4,2), though Blue can retreat first.

### Our plan
Develop Red toward (3,4), then exploit any Blue retreat to increase center control. If Blue remains on (4,3), complete the Yellow pincer from (4,2). Keep same-color capture endpoints distinct and watch for friendly fire within the mixed central formation.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue immediately contested our first central occupation by moving from the right edge to (4,3).

### Lessons
Central occupation can force defensive movement even without an immediate capture. A threatened piece may retreat, so use the gained tempo to strengthen center control.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; Blue holds (4,3). Green advanced to (2,4), blocking a direct Red descent into (3,4). Red is now also at (3,5), so (3,4) lies between two Red pieces, though an opponent may safely move into that static sandwich until a later Red move triggers capture.

### Our plan
If Blue stays on (4,3), use Yellow from (7,2) to (4,2) to sandwich it against Yellow (4,4). If Blue retreats, consider placing a fresh Yellow directly on (4,3) while keeping (4,4). Seek to occupy (3,4) with the developed Red, but account for Green’s ability to enter it first. If Green enters between the Reds, create a move-away-and-return capture tempo when feasible.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contested the lower center immediately. Green then advanced specifically to obstruct Red’s direct reinforcement of the upper center.

### Lessons
A piece moving into an existing sandwich is safe; capture requires a new landing move by the flanking color. Preserve central anchors while developing separate pieces to fill remaining center squares.

### Position read
We hold central squares (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow. Yellow’s move from (7,2) to (4,2) sandwiches and captures Blue at (4,3), leaving that center square empty. Red also stands at (3,5), while Green at (2,4) blocks a direct descent toward (3,4).

### Our plan
Aim to occupy the vacant (4,3) with a Yellow piece while retaining (4,4). For the upper center, develop Red into (3,4) when the route and timing permit. If Green enters (3,4) between Reds at (3,3) and (3,5), remember it is initially safe; arrange a later Red landing that retriggers the sandwich. Protect the two existing central anchors and use separate pieces for completion.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests the lower center but left its piece vulnerable to a same-color Yellow sandwich. Green is obstructing Red’s upper-center reinforcement.

### Lessons
Exploit same-color flanks immediately when available. Static sandwiches do not capture newcomers, so a later triggering move is required.

### Position read
We occupy center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; (4,3) is empty. Green occupies (3,4) between Reds at (3,3) and (3,5), but this static sandwich does not capture. Red moved from (0,4) to (2,4), so Green at (3,4) is now physically boxed on every side by Red at (2,4), (3,3), (3,5) and Yellow at (4,4). It is not enclosed-captured because the adjacent Yellow joins its non-Red group and has liberties.

### Our plan
Keep the boxed Green center blocker immobile while developing Yellow toward (4,3). Seek a safe way to retrigger the Red sandwich on row 3, or surround the mixed Green/Yellow group without sacrificing our center anchor. Preserve Red at (2,4) as the upper block and both row-3 flanks until a concrete capture sequence exists.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests the lower center. Green deliberately entered the static Red sandwich at (3,4), relying on the rule that moving into a sandwich is safe.

### Lessons
Enclosure groups include connected teammate pieces, so Green at (3,4) was not captured when Red landed at (2,4). Occupied squares still immobilize pieces regardless of color.

### Position read
We hold three center squares: Red at (3,3), Yellow at (4,3) and (4,4). Green remains at (3,4), boxed by Red at (2,4), (3,3), (3,5) and Yellow at (4,4), so that piece cannot move. The position is not itself a capture because captures require a qualifying move trigger. Blue has advanced to (1,4) and still contests from the right and lower side.

### Our plan
Preserve the four-piece box around Green and seek a move-triggered capture of the center blocker. If Green is removed, occupying (3,4) immediately wins by center occupation. Avoid casually moving either Red row-3 flank, since that grants Green an escape lane before the flank can return. Develop another Red or Yellow capture mechanism while keeping all three team-held center squares secure.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue is developing toward the central files. Green deliberately entered a static sandwich and is relying on the trigger rule, but is now immobilized.

### Lessons
A boxed piece may remain uncaptured when its mixed non-moving-color enclosure group has liberties. Preserve immobilization until a legal sandwich or enclosure can be triggered.

Red remains at (2,4) and (3,5), boxing (3,4) on three sides, but (3,3) is now an empty liberty. Losses: we have Red 1, Yellow 0; opponent Blue 1, Green 0.

If Green advances (3,2) to (3,3), Red can later land on the vacated (3,2), sandwiching the contiguous Green pieces at (3,3)-(3,4) against (3,5). ### Lessons
Re-evaluate the live board over the prior memo: the former boxed Green escaped indirectly because another Green captured the Red wall at (3,3). Build same-color flanking lines that punish occupation of the resulting gap.

### Position read

Use Red’s next turn to reinforce or attack the upper-center structure while preserving Red at (3,5). We need eventually dislodge Green from (3,4) and refill (4,3). Watch for Green at (3,2) moving away and later returning: returning to (3,2) would sandwich Yellow at (3,3) against Green at (3,4).

The opponent uses move-triggered sandwiches around the center and is developing Blue inward without immediate captures.

### Lessons
Static enemy brackets are harmless until one endpoint moves away and returns. Center occupation creates immediate pressure, but anticipate the opponent’s reset-and-return capture mechanism.

### Position read
We have Red at (0,2), (0,6), (2,3), and (3,5); Yellow holds center squares (3,3) and (4,4). The opponent holds (3,4) with Green and has another Green at (3,2). Losses: our Red 2, Yellow 0; opponent Blue 1, Green 0. One more Red loss causes elimination and conversion to Void.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s turn, consider moving Yellow from (3,3) to (4,3). This opens (3,3) for Red: if Green remains at (3,4), Red can move from (2,3) to (3,3) and sandwich that Green against Red at (3,5). The threat should force Green off (3,4), helping clear the center. Preserve Red at (3,5) as the essential far flank.

The opponent exploits move-triggered sandwiches and recently returned Green to (3,0) to capture our Red at (3,1). Blue is developing inward but has not made an immediate capture.

### Lessons
Coordinate our colors sequentially without treating them as shared sandwich endpoints. Creating a same-color landing-and-flank threat can force a center defender away even when the actual capture is delayed.

### Position read
We have Red at (0,2), (0,6), (2,3), and (3,5); Yellow now occupies adjacent center squares (4,3) and (4,4). The opponent has Green at (3,4) and (3,2), plus Blue developed at (1,3), (3,6), and (5,3). The opponent actively exploits move-triggered sandwiches and has developed Blue pieces inward to constrain central lanes. Green may now move its center defender or disrupt one of the Red endpoints.

### Lessons
A staged threat across consecutive allied turns can force movement even though the two colors cannot flank together. Always recheck whether the opponent’s intervening move breaks the landing path or far endpoint.

Seek one more safe Green capture while protecting fragile Red. Preserve Yellow’s central pair and aim to occupy (3,3) and (3,4), though turns and colors must align. Red’s row-3 formation can create further horizontal traps.

We hold Yellow at center squares (4,3),(4,4), with Red at (3,2),(3,5),(2,3),(0,6). Blue’s active pieces include (1,3),(2,4),(3,7),(6,7).

Pursue a safe third capture against either opponent color. Preserve Yellow’s center pair. Red can potentially enter (3,3), while Yellow can later shift (4,4) to (3,4) and refill it from (7,4), but only if the opponent cannot disrupt the sequence.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has twice allowed direct same-color sandwich tactics. Expect Green to interfere with Yellow’s flank structure or center, and Blue to seek retaliation against fragile Red.

### Lessons
Before each move, scan every friendly aligned pair for enemy chains between them; one-step rook moves often close immediate sandwiches.

Green has 2 losses, Red 2, Yellow 0. Our center remains Yellow at (4,3),(4,4), with Red near the center at (3,2),(2,3),(2,5).

Only Green still needs elimination. Seek one safe Green capture while protecting fragile Red from its third loss. Yellow should preserve the center pair and can pursue center occupation via (3,3) and (3,4), using supporting pieces to refill vacated squares if needed.

The opponent has repeatedly left direct same-color sandwich closures available. Green’s recent move to (5,3) approaches Yellow at (4,3) and may aim to disturb the center. Void Blue can move but cannot capture, so its pieces are blockers and possible walls/flanks only.

Prioritize immediate third-loss captures. After an elimination, distinguish lowercase Void pieces: they remain mobile and count for center occupation but cannot trigger captures.
